# Independent audit: energy supergradient and global positive chart

Audited in full:
`candidate c0fc791108fc8765`.

**PASS, no repair needed.** The canonical finite-hull hypothesis and the
restriction to source points interior to their own fibers are essential
and are retained.

1. Differentiation of the actual attained minimizing integral gives
   grad E=(d+1)E a, hence grad F=((d+1)/d)F a. The parameter Hessian
   is positive definite, so the local implicit-function/envelope
   argument is justified for arbitrary convex bodies. Fixed-body
   concavity then gives the exact lower denominator bound1/(d+1).
2. The support of each real canonical fiber is exactly the finite LP
   maximum over barycentric representations. The dual polyhedron
   has no line because the sampled rows span the base affine hull.
   Its attained minimizing face has a vertex. Each vertex uses one
   of finitely many independent fixed row sets, so uniformly bounded
   input support numbers give a uniform bound on every relevant dual
   slope. Taking minimizing affine functions proves Hausdorff
   Lipschitz control even at boundary bases.
3. The common-radius balls in input fibers give positive full real
   fibers. Near the selected source, Hausdorff control and support
   inequalities give a fixed ball about its continuous coordinate.
   The own optimal denominator bound makes each nearby minimizer
   admissible at the other nearby pair. Testing in both directions,
   bounded integrands, and the dilation bound for symmetric differences
   prove the claimed local Lipschitz energy estimate.
4. Infimal convolution of the convex function -F on the compact convex
   local domain with its Lipschitz norm penalty is a finite convex
   extension agreeing on that domain. Its finite subgradient gives
   the boundary-base support; concavity propagates the local support
   globally. Both signs of continuous displacement force its continuous
   coefficient to be the actual envelope derivative.
5. The displayed affine identity for the chart converts positivity of
   the supporting bracket into L>1/(d+1) on fiber interiors and the
   weak bound on all of C. No energy regularity at boundary marked
   points is assumed.
6. The shorter finite support-majorant proof has the correct sign.
   From h_z(-a)<=h_p(-a)+b.(z-p), adding +b.(z-p) to the source
   denominator cancels the potential negative support excess. Farkas
   uses the actual anchored support inequality. This argument does
   not identify b with an energy supergradient, as explicitly stated.
7. The radius1+sqrt(z) example is a compact convex body with no finite
   boundary energy supergradient, while its canonical sampled hull
   has radius1+z. It correctly separates global-chart admissibility
   from the stronger supergradient interface.

The proved positive chart does not imply a cap payment or a compatible
simultaneous choice at multiple sources. No such consequence is used.
note: Mathematical discussion retained to expose corrections and limitations. This is not a verification run, accepted premise, or approval of the revised submission. Association follows explicit source-document references, not an inferred dependency.
